newsitem.title: UK: Stg, big 1996 crop behind weak UK grains market.
newsitem.headline: Stg, big 1996 crop behind weak UK grains market.

text.p: A strong sterling and a bumper 1996 crop are the underlying factors which have led to the lowest UK grains prices for nearly 20 years, traders and analysts said.
Origin sellers held on to too much of the bumper crop for too long, traders said.
LIFFE July wheat futures bounced off a contract low of 77.00 stg on Monday. On the same day feed wheat for delivery to East Anglia was reported traded at 82.50 stg by brokers.
This is a very different picture to a year ago. In the week ended June 27, 1996, feed wheat for July 1996 delivery to East Anglia was reported done at 115 stg, down from 119.50 a week earlier.
Final Ministry of Agriculture estimates put the total UK 1996 grains crop at 24.58 million tonnes, including 16.1 million tonnes of wheat, 7.78 million of barley and 590,000 tonnes of oats.
This compares with a total of 21.86 million tonnes in 1995, including 14.31 million of wheat and 6.83 of barley.
